chapter: Movies and the Los Angeles scene
title: Hour-long jam sessions, stamina and cheating on fast tempos
summary: They played one tune like I've Got Rhythm for an hour, with Nat Cole and Lee Young; Stewart now sometimes plays in two to save his arm.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Now, in these sessions did you all tend to play longer solos than, say, on records. I mean like sessions.
Oh, yes, we would play sometimes two and three choruses on different things. We'd play and -- and I can remember playing even one number, 'I've Got Rhythm,' for maybe about an hour or so.
Oh, in that particular session?
Sure.
Oh, that's --
Sure.
Did the piano player switch over on that, I mean like --
Oh, yes, piano, we had piano, and even Nat played a couple of things with the groups, the horn blowers,
Jimmy and myself. I think one fellow, Lee Young, brought his drum set. We had a regular session then, out there.
So like -- when you -- so at that time you and Blanton didn't have any -- you all's stamina was up where you could play for an hour without --
Oh, sure, yes. Yes, youngsters, you know.
(Laughter.)
That must have been quite a sound.

Plucking, and that arm was really flying you know, and being young, of course -- I couldn't do it now quite as much as I did at that time. I still have a little power in my arms and my hands, you know, where I can pluck with, but every once in a while I have to cheat a little bit, you know, yeah.
When you say cheat a little bit, what do you mean?
I mean instead of plucking four time real fast, every once in a while I play two.
Oh, yeah, yeah, I've heard a lot of things played two --
Yeah, sure, instead of that fast 4/4.
Right. Sometimes they play -- guys will play a pedal too, just sit one place and go boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom --
That's right, yeah.
But it's -- stay one place.
(Laughter.)
Sure.
And they say, you all got it, you know.
Sure.
So do you remember who some of the other player -- the horn players were at that particular session?
Well, I think Rex Stewart was on the scene at that party. Oh, let me think. It's -- oh, let's see. This was in the mid-'40s, you know. And --
Actually it was the early '40s, because I think Blanton was dead in '42.
Yeah. Well, it would have to be the early '40s, maybe 1940, yeah.
You see --
I can't think of some of the other musicians. But every once in a while we -- the cats used to get together, and especially after the Lovejoy's, the home of the Big Leg Chicken, you know --
Yeah, right up in there.
And that was the spot.
